name: Chthonic-Threnody
description: Glacier upon glacier, blue-white and creaking, buried in places by nitrogen snow. The shell is broken in places by a subterranean ocean, and through those breaches the deep ocean breathes plumes of frost into the dark.
The air carries cold salt and iodine, and sound behaves strangely: footsteps crack loud, then die without echo. At night the temperature drops fast enough to hear the rock tick as it contracts.
Geologists argue about the strata here: several layers appear deposited out of order, as if the planet's history were shuffled like cards.
The charts mark this world in cautious amber. Those who ignore the marking tend to come back rich, changed, or not at all.
